The test is about CMAESOptimizer throwing a NumberIsTooLargeException when the boundaries for optimization variables are too large (around half of Double.MAX_VALUE in magnitude). The bug report says that when large boundaries (like -Double.MAX_VALUE and Double.MAX_VALUE) are passed to the optimizer, the internal encoding/decoding of parameters to normalized form causes NaN values in the parameters sent to the fitness function. This is likely because the difference between the lower and upper bound is exceedingly large and when used for normalization, it causes overflow or nonsensical values (NaN).

This bug report and test seem to hint that the root problem lies in the encoding and decoding of the parameters from the normalized space back to the original bounds space inside CMAESOptimizer or its base classes. The overflow or NaN happens during these transformations because the range between bounds is beyond the representable limits of double precision.

I tried to locate the code for CMAESOptimizer.optimize(int, MultivariateFunction, GoalType, double[], double[], double[]) but there are multiple possible matches across the inheritance hierarchy with unclear resolution.

Next step: I will try to find the code for parameter normalization or encoding/decoding of parameters in CMAESOptimizer or its base classes around handling of bounds arrays, looking for methods called encode/decode or normalization logic that uses the difference of upper and lower bounds in arithmetic operations that can overflow to NaN. This will help confirm the cause explained in the bug report and test.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
